title: Anisotropic dynamical reconstruction of quantum geometry in quenched Chern insulators
authors: Nan Li, Zhiyong Liu, Zhaoxin Liang, Ying Hu
abstract: Under unitary dynamics, the Chern number of an evolving quantum state remains conserved even when a quench drives the Hamiltonian across a topological phase transition. In sharp contrast, we reveal an anisotropic dynamical reconstruction of the quantum metric. Following a sudden quench in a two-dimensional Chern insulator, the metric develops a principal frame in which one eigenvalue grows in time whereas the other remains nearly unchanged. At long times, the associated axes align with the energy-gradient direction and the tangent direction of the constant-energy contours of the post-quench Hamiltonian, respectively. This dynamically selected frame is distinct from that of the static post-quench ground-state metric. We identify momentum-dependent relative dynamical phases as its origin: they enhance the distinguishability of neighboring states separated along the energy-gradient direction, while states along an equal-energy contour remain nearly phase locked. Consequently, local and global metric observables acquire characteristic long-time signatures of the post-quench Hamiltonian. Our results establish a nonequilibrium mechanism by which coherent dynamics reorganizes quantum geometry, suggesting new possibilities for its dynamical control.
summary: This work analyzes how the quantum geometry of a Chern insulator evolves after a sudden quench, finding that while the topological invariant (Chern number) is conserved, the quantum metric undergoes a distinct anisotropic reconstruction. This reorganization is driven by momentum-dependent relative dynamical phases, causing the metric's principal axes to align with the energy-gradient and constant-energy contour directions of the final Hamiltonian.
main_problem: The study investigates how the quantum metric of a coherently evolving quantum state reorganizes during unitary dynamics, particularly following a sudden quench, contrasting this with the conserved topological invariant (Chern number).
main_result: The quantum metric undergoes an anisotropic dynamical reconstruction, where the principal axes align with the energy-gradient and the tangent direction of the constant-energy contours of the post-quench Hamiltonian.
method: The authors calculate the time evolution of the quantum metric tensor and its principal axes using the time-dependent polarization vector derived from the quench dynamics.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using a two-dimensional (2D) massive Dirac model, serving as a paradigmatic Chern insulator, subjected to a sudden quench from an initial to a final Hamiltonian.
key_observables:
Quantum metric tensor ($G_{\mu
u}(\mathbf{k}, t)$), quantum volume ($	ext{vol}_g$), Wannier spread ($\Omega_I$), and the Chern number ($C(t)$).
important_parameters: The quench time and the parameters defining the initial and final Hamiltonians (e.g., mass parameter $m$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on unitary dynamics and the assumption that the system can be described by the time-dependent polarization vector $\hat{n}(\mathbf{k}, t)$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the static quantum geometry (Chern number, volume, Wannier spread) and show the time evolution of the quantum-volume density, demonstrating the anisotropic growth of the metric components.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the conservation of the Chern number while analyzing the time evolution of the quantum metric. It then details the anisotropic reconstruction, showing how the principal axes align with specific geometric directions dictated by the post-quench Hamiltonian, which is attributed to momentum-dependent relative dynamical phases.
why_interesting: The concept of dynamically selected geometric structures (like the principal axes of the metric) that are distinct from the static ground state is highly relevant for understanding non-equilibrium quantum dynamics in condensed matter systems.
